inventedEvidence.evidence: 'A completely dead machine with power at the wall' - the customer never confirmed power at the machine's socket or spur, only that the kettle and fridge work

confidentUnsupported.evidence: 'usually indicates an internal fault, such as a failed mains filter on the circuit board'

rationale: The assistant never asked the obvious first check for an integrated machine - whether there is a switched spur/isolator above the worktop or a tripped breaker at the consumer unit - which was the actual cause. Instead it ignored the customer's statement that the plug was inaccessible, told her to 'switch it off and unplug it' then 'pull the machine out', pushed for a model number with a replacement-part panel, and finally declared an internal mains-filter fault needing an engineer. The final confident diagnosis is unsupported by the evidence and would have sent a renter to an engineer callout for a switch that was simply off; no mention of the landlord either.
